Appearance:
MR MAULIK S SHETH(3586) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 NOTICE SERVED BY DS for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MS CM SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ================================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ILESH J. VORA  Date : 14/03/2024

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

By invoking inherent jurisdiction of this Court, the applicant - original accused No.2 Bijal Manubhai Barot, is seeking quashing of the FIR being No.111960117220335 of 2022 registered with Panigate Police Station, Vadodara for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 114 of IPC.
2.
This Court has heard learned counsel Mr. Mohit Pathak for learned counsel Mr. Maulik S. Sheth and learned APP Ms. Chetna M. Shah for the respondent - State.
The respondent No.2-Dipak Madhubhai Srivastav, who has lodged the FIR, though served, has not chosen to remain present in the proceedings nor filed any reply affidavit.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15041/2022 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined Bijal Manubhai Barot vs State Of Gujarat on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113528589/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 3. Brief facts giving rise to file to the present application are that the applicant is the wife of accused No.1-Kirtan Bharat Rao.

The accused had entered into limited liability partnerships agreement and the name of the firm was MACROSCOSM LLP LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP FIRM and the firm was created to provide services and selling health products etc.

entities.text: MACROSCOSM LLP LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP FIRM
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Respondent No.2 came into contact with the accused No.1 as he wanted to purchase Car of the Morris Garage Company.

The accused No.1 promised for that he will arrange the said car with substantial discount and based on the said promise, the respondent No.2 paid Rs.20 Lakh/- through RTGS and by account payee cheque.
Despite the payment made by the complainant, the accused No.1 could not deliver the car in time and on asking the refund of the amount, he failed to repay the same.
In such circumstances, the FIR for cheating and criminal breach of trust was being lodged against the accused No.1 and his wife.

4. Learned counsel Mr. Mohit Pathak appearing for the applicant accused No.2, Bijal Barot has submitted that the proceeding of the FIR qua the accused No.1 has been quashed by this Court as respondent No.2 and accused NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15041/2022 ORDER DATED:
14/03/2024 undefined No.1 settled their disputes.
He would further urged that the applicant herein was not a active partner of the firm and she did not have knowledge about the said transaction and had never received any benefit direct or indirect.
He would further urged that the applicant being a formal partner has been impleaded as accused and she has nothing to do with the alleged promise given by her husband.
Lastly, he would submits that due to matrimonial disputes the applicant is living separately and matrimonial proceedings are pending before the Court concerned.

In such circumstances, when the FIR against the principal accused has been quashed and considering the role attributed to the present applicant herein, the continuation of the proceedings would nothing but a sheer harassment to her and thus therefore same may be quashed and set aside.
5.

Learned APP Ms. Chetna M. Shah has submitted that the applicant was partner of the firm and the amount was credited in the partnership firm and thus therefore she equally liable for the alleged act of breach of trust and cheating and thus therefore she would urged that no case is made out for exercising the powers of this Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15041/2022 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined 6.
As observed, the respondent No.2 though served did not remain present.
It is not in dispute that the criminal proceedings qua the applicant No.1 has been quashed by this Court as the respondent No.2 gave his consent in quashing the FIR.
The matrimonial disputes of the applicant with the accused No.1 is going on.

In such circumstances when the questioned FIR is quashed against the principal accused who had pocketed the alleged amount, the continuation of the criminal proceedings qua the applicant will not serve any purpose as the respondent No.2 is not interested to pursue the proceedings.

7. For the reasons recorded and considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case,
this court is convinced that the case is made out to exercise inherent powers of this court, and therefore, to prevent the misuse of process of law, the questioned FIR deserves to be quashed and set aside and is hereby quashed.
The application is allowed.

The FIR mentioned in Para-1 of the Bijal Manubhai Barot vs State Of Gujarat on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113528589/
2 order and consequential proceedings thereto are hereby quashed against the applicant.
